title: A.I. Art Assets, are you using them? How are you using them?
author: postedbyai
selftext:
[asked this about a week ago](https://www.reddit.com/r/gamedev/comments/117vy4o/ai_art_assets_are_you_using_them_how_are_you/) in /r/gamedev but figured there might be more detailed response here.

Been  playing A LOT with A.I. Art but besides some UV texture experiments and  some jet fighters, and some 'badges' that could probably make a decent  space invader, I'm not sure where AI art assets come into play.

I  see a lot of struggle to make pixel art but they all end up as static  character images that are clearly rendered at least double the size  they'll end being used.

Whose doing what? What's the workflow?

comments.author: DG_BlueOnyx
comments.body:
A quick use that anyone can do is updating Asset store 2d/3d textures to look more unique using controlnet.  
\-  
Most of the workload time I have spent is on stylized backdrops though.

Using AI assistance for backdrops in the old pre-rendered style.  
[https://postimg.cc/y3FJ4HLp](https://postimg.cc/y3FJ4HLp)  
\-  
Each image is something like 12-20 hours of inpainting, and photoshop work.  
\-  
it then gets brought into unity, where I add bloom, and dithering, and shaders for foliage movement, and overlay areas.  
[https://postimg.cc/1nYxmnjf](https://postimg.cc/1nYxmnjf)

replies.author: postedbyai
replies.body: That sure is a big outpaint. What do you do it with A1111? Gimp? InvokeAI?

replies.author: DG_BlueOnyx
replies.body:
i'm on a 1050 TI gpu so a lot of my workflow is A1111 on Colab using Fast Bens  
[https://colab.research.google.com/github/TheLastBen/fast-stable-diffusion/blob/main/fast\_stable\_diffusion\_AUTOMATIC1111.ipynb](https://colab.research.google.com/github/TheLastBen/fast-stable-diffusion/blob/main/fast_stable_diffusion_AUTOMATIC1111.ipynb)  
\-  
Typically start off with 768 X 512 image, and expand it out in photoshop if needed.I don't usually use outpainting, but just increase the resolution in photoshop, smudge out the sides how I think it should look, and inpaint the new smudged region.  
\-  
Most images sorta start off like a blob like this, and I do the individual parts.[https://postimg.cc/dLyCznwp](https://postimg.cc/dLyCznwp)  
\-  
once it's near perfect, I upscale it, and clean up the artifacting in A111 and photoshop.

replies.author: fisj
replies.body: Really awesome work! Have you tried kitbashing most of the 3d assets into the layout first and then inpainting and style transferring to get precisely what you want? This seems pretty flexible, depending on whether you're more comfortable with 2d, vs. 3d.

replies.author: DG_BlueOnyx
replies.body:
I've utilized 3D objects when SD just kept failing at a simple object.  Typically from a screenshot of blender, or Unity.  
\-  
And the Unity scenes include a lot of 3D objects for motion, like cloth, and windmills.  With a shader that sorta blends with the colors of the background a bit.  
\-  
I like the idea of having cutscenes at some point, so will likely have a model of vehicles, and specific buildings that might end up getting inpainted into a background just to make it look a bit nicer than a 3d object popping out.

comments.author: fisj
comments.body:
I'm mostly just trying to keep ontop of the news and updates. A lot of what I'm doing right now is mapping out possible workflows. Theory crafting as it were.

I put together a little mindmap last night to organize my thoughts.

There's asset generation, there's runtime simulation, there's editor tools like the marioGPT stuff we saw last week, and lastly there's AI in the creative process, where AI can assist devs in being more efficient in exploring ideas, concepting visually, doing research on history etc.

Hypothetically speaking. I will not be using AI assets until there's a bit more legal grounding. I'm in the fortunate position where I can happily make the art myself.

3D advances are going to be an interesting area. If you look at the data available for 2d art versus 3D, there's a shortfall of several orders of magnitude. Its possible stable diffusion might be able to make progress faster towards 3D, via turn tables of a character, and then using a photogrammetric technique, or via a differentiable rendering route.

There's a lot of pieces of workflows, or tantalizing bits floating around, but nothing production ready ... but thats half the fun.

&#x200B;

replies.author: postedbyai
replies.body:
Thanks for the analysis. I've tested Point-E it was horrible. I've tested AI UV mapping it was horrible. 

Clearly the US copyright office has no intention of protecting AI art so any textures, 3D models generated with the AI will not be protected. 

UNLESS someone comes up with a way to embed a computer program in such a way that it generates the model/art then the program will be protected by copyright, so  a ultra-portable asset browser/generator data model has to become the default.

comments.author: PolyhiveHQ
comments.body: Some friends and I have built a tool that allows you to texture 3D assets using a text prompt. The hope is that these AI textured models could be either ready to go in your game, or a great starting point for further manual improvement. You can check it out here: https://polyhive.ai/ai

comments.author: willcodeforbread
comments.body:
I'm not using AI Art assets, as I can make art already, but I am looking at AI to help with my tooling and workflows.

E.g. just recently I was exploring using ML to help with lerping animation frames, or producing effects like "line boil" (the latter benefited more from good old shader tech in the end).

And then possibly training a GPT language model for GDScript (Godot), if it doesn't exist already, just to get some co-pilot-like speed-ups in the editor. (That said, I'm just thinking about this, and don't "need" it yet, as game scripting is a fairly light thing anyway, with most of the functionality already encapsulated in the nodes.)

I tried GPT for co-designing some game mechanics and narratives, but it didn't come up with anything that I couldn't do myself. I've tweeted this exact sentiment a few times already: GPT can't dream and ideate like us humans do (at least not yet), and is just a copycat so far.

EDIT: you might be interested in following this project: https://echoesofsomewhere.com/
